title: DevOps Center - The New Deployment Tool - Sigma Infosolutions
body: # DevOps Center – The New Deployment Tool. DevOps Center, a recent addition to Salesforce applications, is designed to eventually replace change sets in its functionalities. The game-changer for Salesforce teams is that the DevOps Center manages the source control branch so you can focus on development tasks. However, it’s important to note that eventually, Salesforce is likely to retire change sets altogether in favor of the DevOps Center. **DevOps Center** significantly improves the change and release management process when developing with Salesforce. * **Organize your work:** Work Items, a new object designed for the DevOps Center and open to standard Salesforce Flows and other operations, can be used to track and deploy the associated changes. **Creating a new Work Item**. ## Work Item Stages:. Work Item Stages in DevOps Center Salesforce are the different phases that a work item goes through as it is developed, tested, and deployed to production. When you click ‘Create Review,’ the work item transitions to the ‘In Review’ status, and an automatic change request is generated. This work item advances to a pipeline stage, and upon reaching the final stage, it transitions to the Closed status. To incorporate metadata changes into the Work Item, you have two alternatives:. Clicking it transitions the Work Item to the ‘**In Review**‘ stage, simultaneously creating a pull request in the backend. After initiating a pull request, you can designate it as ‘**Ready to Promote**,’ enabling the Work Item for promotion to the next stage in the pipeline. And there you have it, the Work Item has been successfully deployed! After a successful promotion, the Work Item will transition automatically to the **Closed** stage. ## Change Work Item Status to Never:. If a change conflicts, removing files from the commit can ensure successful promotions of other work items. When you change the status to Never, the work item becomes inactive, and the committed component files are returned to the list of available changes. You can change a work item’s status to Never before it’s been promoted into a pipeline stage. From the work item menu, select **Change Status to Never**, then click **Confirm**.

Launched in stealth last year, LibLab provides SDK development tools that integrate with an API for authentication, error handling, security and more. Beyond this, LibLab monitors and updates the SDK "when the language evolves," according to Ofek, and shows metrics that indicate how the API is being used. Our core engine will be open source so developers can contribute and make our SDK generator better with time. Nearly 38% of M&A deals globally in the AI & ML sector had a venture-backed buyer in 2025—higher than the 31% share for M&A across all industries, according to PitchBook data. Anthropic’s recent acquisition of Vercept, an agentic AI startup, is the latest in a trend of well-capitalized AI companies doing everything they can to move fast and remain competitive. Of the 702 M&A deals globally for AI & ML startups in 2025, 283 transactions were led by VC-backed buyers, accounting for 37.5%. title: AI Agent Company Decagon Held Early M&A Talks With ServiceNow, Others - Business Insider
body: Buzzy AI agent startup Decagon could be the latest company swept up in a growing wave of AI dealmaking. The company, which was last valued at $4.5 billion earlier this year, has hired a bank to evaluate acquisition interest, according to people familiar with the matter. The interest in Decagon represents a new shift in the AI boom: after years of huge venture rounds and soaring valuations, tech companies are increasingly looking to buy their way into promising AI markets. Growing AI-related businesses are often getting offers at a significant premium to their last valuation, so if Decagon were to accept an offer, it could be considerably higher than its previous $4.5 billion value. It competes with industry veteran Bret Taylor's Sierra, which was valued at $15.8 billion earlier this year. It was also punished for making a $7 billion acquisition of the security business Armis, a deal announced late last year.

title: The VC Landscape In 2025: Key Trends That Shaped The Year - Forbes
body: Venture capital firms are chasing AI deals with unprecedented intensity, often at eye-watering valuations. According to the SVB Innovative Economy Outlook, for the first time more mega-deal dollars flowed into AI companies ($73 billion) than into non-AI companies ($47 billion). *“Capital is consolidating because AI companies have scaled incredibly fast and achieved outsized outcomes with far smaller teams relative to the capital they raise,”* explains Michelle Kwok, Principal at Draper Associates. According to Dimitriy Mishin, venture investor and serial entrepreneur, key portfolio companies include You.com, Reflection AI, Sent.dm, Tahcar, Anyroad, Watt Data and WalkWay AI. The firm also increased exposure to AI-focused funds such as AiX Ventures and Day One Ventures. Other notable mega-rounds went to companies like **Fervo Energy**, **Boom Supersonic** and **Fal**, which raised $140 million for its generative AI platform. PE firms are increasingly investing in later-stage, venture-backed companies—and in some cases, “eating VC’s lunch.”.

title: Skild AI worth $14B, Airwallex's Series G, and BioMatrix makes a buy. - Axios
body: • **Skild AI**, a Pittsburgh-based AI robotics company, is in talks to raise more than $1b in Series C funding at an approximately $14b valuation from **SoftBank** and **Nvidia**, per Reuters. • **Airwallex**, an Australia-based payments firm, raised US$330m in Series G funding at an $8b valuation. • **Resemble AI**, a deepfakes detection startup, raised $13m from Google's AI Future Fund, Okta Ventures, Taiwania Capital, Gentree Fund, IAG Capital Partners, Berkeley Frontier Fund, and KDDI. • **Rotostitch**, an SF-based textile manufacturing tech startup, raised $1m in pre-seed funding led by **Boost VC** and **Nova Threshold**. • **Harbor IT,** a Brazilian managed IT services provider, acquired **ZAG Technical Services**, a San Jose, Calif.-based cybersecurity services company. • **Millman**, a Seattle-based consulting firm, acquired **MorVest Capital**, a Port O'Connor, Texas-based mortgage servicing rights analytics company. • **Andersen Group**, an SF-based tax advisory formed by former Arthur Andersen partners, set IPO terms to 11m shares at $14-$16.

title: Beyond US tech: The global semiconductor opportunity | VettaFi
body:
The International Semiconductor industry is experiencing historic growth driven largely by the boom in AI infrastructure demand. According to Deloitte, the global semiconductor industry is expected to reach $975 billion in annual revenue in 2026, representing a historical peak. It is expected to become a $1 trillion industry by next year.

The VettaFi International Semiconductor Index offers exposure to the top 25 non-US semiconductor and semiconductor equipment manufacturers. [...] Despite its favorable diversification, growth, and fundamental characteristics, international semiconductor exposure is not without its risks. The top 25 international semiconductor and capital equipment companies have a high geographic concentration in East Asia (Taiwan, South Korea, and China), which leaves them vulnerable to trade tensions and geopolitical risks. With respect to China specifically, US-China export controls create short-term challenges. However, they simultaneously catalyze [...] As rapid expansion among global hyperscalers and data centers strains worldwide capacity, international semiconductor and equipment manufacturers play an increasingly critical role in supporting the global supply chain. Key international suppliers are seeing record order bookings and multi-year backlogs.
